rationale: The golden_rejected issue is present: the golden submission fails SR4 in the differential golden_run (exit_code=1, expected pass). SR1, SR2, SR3, SR5 all pass; only SR4 fails. Per validation_report.issues[0].issue == 'golden_rejected' and analyzer confirms the golden RTL/ground-truth is coherent and the golden submission itself is well-reasoned and structurally sound (per analyzer requirement_results, coherence check passes). The failure is localized to the SR4 checker's implementation: it requires a SINGLE top-2 candidate to combine the trigger-condition pattern with either bit-3 corruption OR mismatch-masking language in the same candidate's text, but the golden (and the participant-facing README) explicitly recommend splitting the trigger, the result-corruption payload, and the mismatch-masking payload into separate distinct candidates. This causes a correct, well-structured, high-confidence submission to be rejected, making the benchmark unusable as shipped. Because mutation testing is blocked until the baseline (golden) run passes, mutation_score=0.0 is not meaningful and cannot be used to judge discrimination quality. The evaluation_framework must be repaired before this case can be retained.
revision_instructions:
Fix the SR4 check in evaluate.py (the ranking/confidence-calibration requirement). Do NOT require a single top-2 candidate to simultaneously match both the trigger-condition pattern and (bit-3-corruption OR mismatch-masking) language in the same candidate string. Instead, evaluate SR4 by checking whether the SET/UNION of the top-N highest-confidence candidates (at least those with confidence >= 0.6, or the top 2-3 by confidence, whichever is more permissive) collectively satisfies: (a) at least one high-confidence candidate satisfies the SR1 trigger-identification criterion, AND (b) at least one high-confidence candidate (possibly the same or a different one) satisfies the SR2 bit-3-corruption criterion OR the SR3 mismatch-masking criterion. In other words, allow the trigger, the data-corruption payload, and the integrity-masking payload to be reported as separate, individually high-confidence candidates rather than forcing them into one candidate's rationale text. The check must still enforce that a truly buried or low-confidence correct finding (e.g. all relevant candidates ranked below confidence 0.5 or below the top few slots) fails SR4 — the intent is to penalize genuinely low-ranked correct answers, not to penalize reasonable per-node candidate splitting. After the fix, re-run the golden submission and confirm all [TEST] PASS lines including SR4, then re-run the full differential and mutation suite to obtain a meaningful mutation_score before resubmission.

Additionally, address the analyzer's secondary recommendation: evaluate.py currently only emits aggregate PASS/FAIL per requirement without computing the four declared continuous metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, trigger_payload_localization, confidence_calibration) from the task spec's evaluation.metrics section. Add explicit computation and output of these four metrics based on the graded requirement outcomes and candidate confidence/ranking so they are actually measured, not just implied by pass/fail.
